agent_notes: Verb forms in 147:12 are feminine singular (shabbechi, halli, -ikh), addressed to the city. Hebrew verse 12 corresponds to the beginning of Psalm 147 in the Greek (LXX) and Vulgate, whose numbering is one behind from Ps 10 to 147 and splits this psalm here (LXX 146 / 147). KJV follows the Hebrew numbering, so there is no difference in verse numbers inside this window.

The verbs are perfects (chizzaq, berakh). Radak and Meiri read them as promises told in the past tense, as prophecy often does; KJV, YLT and ASV take them as accomplished fact. I kept the perfect in the literal layer and let the dramatic layer read them as settled fact, which fits the city-and-gates setting.

chelev chittim is literally 'fat of wheat'. Rashi and Radak read it as the best of the wheat; Metzudat Zion cites Gen 45:18 for chelev as 'the best'. I kept 'fat' in the literal layer and 'finest' in the dramatic one.

history.note: [consider] Separate the two: Metzudat David and Radak take whiteness, Meiri takes softness. (Metzudat David on PS.147.16: "לבן כצמר ... על כי אין מה בארץ יותר לבן מצמר"; Meiri: "אלא שהדמיון לרכותו".)

agent_notes: kefittim ('like crumbs') is disputed. Radak and Metzudat Zion take pat as 'pieces' (Lev 2:6, 'break it into pieces'). BBE's 'raindrops' has no footing in the Hebrew. I follow the 'crumbs/morsels' reading. Rashi's aggadic reading, which I mention only in passing, is not needed for the sense.

Verses 15-18 use 'his word' (dvaro, imrato) for the cause of weather. Ibn Ezra reads yashev as a hiphil of nashav, 'blow'. The Targum's 'his heat' for 'his word' in v. 18 is a different reading; I do not follow it.
The Ketiv in the packet shows dvaro (singular) with a Qere dvarav (plural). I glossed the plural, which matches the parallel 'his statutes and his judgments'.

agent_notes: «חלב חטים» — «тук пшеницы» у Синодального перевода; в драматическом слое выбрано «самое сердце пшеницы» в духе английского слоя, в буквальном — «тук пшеницы».
Нумерация стихов здесь еврейская, как в корпусе; в Синодальном переводе стихи этого псалома могут быть сдвинуты, поэтому цитаты из него даны по смыслу, а не по номеру.
Синодальный перевод передаёт «קרחו» словом «град» («Бросает град Свой кусками»); в буквальном слое оставлен «лёд», как в иврите и в английском слое. Об этом сказано в комментарии.
